headline: House rejected a resolution that would have ended the 2012 national emergency blocking property of people threatening Yemen's peace and stability.
what_it_does: This resolution would have ended a national emergency that President Obama declared on May 16, 2012, about Yemen. That emergency lets the government block the property of certain people found to threaten the peace, security, or stability of Yemen. Ending the emergency would have removed the legal basis for those property blocks. The House voted it down on July 18, 2023.

who_it_affects.group: People and groups named under the Yemen sanctions program
who_it_affects.how: Their blocked property in the U.S. could have been released if the emergency ended.
They would no longer have been required to freeze or refuse dealings with property of people covered by the Yemen sanctions.

who_it_affects.group: The President and federal agencies that enforce sanctions
who_it_affects.how: They would have lost this emergency-based authority to block property tied to threats against Yemen.
